facts.text: Bayesian methods combine prior beliefs with test results to produce an updated belief; sequential testing permits early stopping once evidence is clearly good or clearly bad.
facts.quote: Bayesian methods combine what you believed before the test (the prior) with the test results to produce an updated belief, and sequential testing lets you stop testing early once the evidence is clearly good or clearly bad.

facts.text: For braking-system validation, thousands of simulation runs could provide a Bayesian prior that a few hundred physical trials update, potentially reducing the physical sample below what the rule of three alone demands.
facts.quote: thousands of simulation runs could serve as the prior, and a few hundred physical trials would update it, so the physical sample could be smaller than the rule of three alone demands.

facts.text: Bayesian braking-system validation results are very sensitive to the strength of the prior.
facts.quote: The booklet warns that the result is very sensitive to the strength of the prior.

facts.text: A conservative Bayesian analysis of autonomous-vehicle road testing in 2019 found that a strong prior with 90 percent prior confidence reduced the RAND requirement from 275 million fatality-free miles to 69 million.
facts.quote: A conservative Bayesian analysis of autonomous-vehicle road testing (2019) found that a strong prior with 90 percent prior confidence cut the RAND requirement of 275 million fatality-free miles to 69 million

facts.text: A conservative Bayesian analysis of autonomous-vehicle road testing in 2019 found that a weak prior increased the RAND requirement from 275 million fatality-free miles to 476 million.
facts.quote: the RAND requirement of 275 million fatality-free miles to 69 million, while a weak prior raised it to 476 million.

facts.text: Conservative Bayesian methods should be used for braking-system validation because assessors will challenge the prior.
facts.quote: Assessors will challenge the prior, so conservative methods should be used [Chapter 9].

facts.text: A sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) checks evidence after each trial or batch and stops testing as soon as the result is clearly above or below the required level.
facts.quote: In a sequential probability ratio test (SPRT), the evidence is checked after each trial or batch, and testing stops as soon as the result is clearly above or below the required level.

facts.text: Sequential testing saves trials, making sequential testing attractive for the braking-system program's four-month validation window.
facts.quote: This saves trials, which is attractive in a four-month window

facts.text: Sequential-testing stopping rules must be fixed in advance; stopping merely when the numbers look good invalidates the statistical approach.
facts.quote: the stopping rules must be fixed in advance; stopping when the numbers happen to look good cheats the statistics [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Experts disagree about Bayesian priors from simulation: proponents report large reductions in physical testing, while critics emphasize sensitivity to the prior.
facts.quote: The booklet lists "Bayesian priors from simulation" among the points where experts disagree: proponents report large reductions in physical testing, critics point to the prior sensitivity.

facts.text: Any Bayesian combination of simulation and physical-test evidence depends on a documented credibility assessment of the simulation.
facts.quote: Any Bayesian combination also depends on a documented credibility assessment of the simulation [Chapter 9].
